exampleAnswers.title: Domains of Functions With Reciprocal and Radical Components

question.text: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf f(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \sqrt{t+1} \\ e^t \\ 2t \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
To find the domain of $\mathbf{f},$ we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

  • The domain of $\sqrt{t+1} $ is $t \in [-1,\infty).$

  • The domain of $e^t$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

  • The domain of $2t$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(t)$ is $t \in [-1,\infty).$

question.text: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf f(t) = \left\langle 5t, \: \dfrac{1}{(t+2)^2}, \: e^{t}+t \right\rangle.$
question.explanation:
To find the domain of $\mathbf{f}$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

  • The domain of the 1st component $5t$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

  • The domain of the 2nd component $\dfrac{1}{(t+2)^2}$ is $t \in (-\infty,-2)\cup(-2,\infty).$

  • The domain of the 3rd component $e^{t}+t$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(t)$ is $t \in (-\infty, -2) \cup (-2, \infty).$

exampleAnswers.title: Domains of Functions With Trigonometric Components

question.text: The domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf f (t) = \cot(2t) \, \mathbf i + \cos {t} \,\mathbf j + (t^3 +1) \,\mathbf k$ is \[ t\in (-\infty,\infty), \quad t \neq \bbox[5pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}. \] What is the missing expression? You may assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
To find the domain of $\mathbf{f}$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

  • The domain of the 1st component $\cot(2t)$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty),$ except for the values of $t$ for which \[ 2t = \pi n \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad t = \dfrac{\pi n}{2}, \] where $n$ is an integer.

  • The domain of the 2nd component $\cos{t}$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

  • The domain of the 3rd component $t^3+1$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(t)$ is \[ t\in (-\infty,\infty), \quad t \neq \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\dfrac{\pi n}{2}}, \] where $n$ is an integer.

example.title: Domains of Functions With Trigonometric Components

question.text: The domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf f (t) = \sec\left( t+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) \, \mathbf i + e^{t-1} \,\mathbf j + t^2 \,\mathbf k$ is \[ t\in (-\infty,\infty), \quad t \neq \bbox[5pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}. \] What is the missing expression? You may assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
To find the domain of $\mathbf{f}$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

  • The domain of the 1st component $ \sec\left( t+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty),$ except for the values of $t$ for which \[ t + \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \pi n \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad t =\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \pi n, \] where $n$ is an integer.

  • The domain of the 2nd component $e^{t-1}$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

  • The domain of the 3rd component $t^2$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(t)$ is \[ t\in (-\infty,\infty), \quad t \neq \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\dfrac{\pi}{4} +\pi n }, \] where $n$ is an integer.
